statement: The 2D plastic bending example 2DplasticBending.py uses a 2D plane-strain modeling space (fd.ModelingSpace("2Dplane")) with NLGEOM = True and default typeBending = "3nodes".
2DplasticBending.py defines the plate with E = 200e3 MPa, L = 16 mm, h = 2 mm, nu = 0.3 and imposed top displacement uimp = -5.
In 2DplasticBending.py the mat=0 branch creates an elastic material with the (typo) name "Constitu1tiveLaw", while mat=1 uses Simcoon EPICP with power-law hardening (Re = 300, k = 1000, m = 0.25).
2DplasticBending.py solves step 1 with pb.nlsolve(dt=0.05, tmax=1, update_dt=True, tol_nr=0.05, interval_output=0.05).

In step 2 of 2DplasticBending.py the top Dirichlet BC is removed, replaced by a zero Neumann force started at the previous external force (relaxation), and the NR criterion is set to "Force" with adaptive_stiffness=True plus add_line_search().
The from-scratch variant uses a hand-coded manual Newton-Raphson loop (not pb.nlsolve) with 20 time increments, tol_nr = 0.05 and max_subiter = 5, on the same 2Dplane/nlgeom=False model.
The from-scratch variant builds the weak form with StressEquilibrium("ConstitutiveLaw", nlgeom=False).
The 3D plastic bending example uses a 3D box_mesh (21x7x7 nodes, hex8), imposed top displacement uimp = -8, and StressEquilibrium with NLGEOM ("UL") and incompressibility="fbar".
In plastic_bending_3D.py the mat==2 branch uses native fedoo ElastoPlasticity with a power hardening function (set_hardening_function("power", h=k, beta=m), k=1000, m=0.3).
plastic_bending_3D.py sets the NR criterion to "Force" (tol=5e-3, max_subiter=16) and solves with nlsolve(dt=0.025, tmax=1).
The elasto_plasticity.py module is documented as J2 plasticity with isotropic hardening, additive on the strain measure.
ElastoPlasticity is a subclass of MechanicalUMAT whose stress integration uses a vectorized radial-return algorithm for the von Mises yield criterion.
The ElastoPlasticity constructor registers n_statev=7 with statev labels {"P": 0, "EP": slice(1,7)} (scalar accumulated plastic strain P and 6-component plastic-strain tensor EP).
ElastoPlasticity.get_elastic_matrix raises NotImplementedError for the plane-stress "2Dstress" dimension, directing users to a Simcoon plasticity law such as Simcoon("EPICP").
ElastoPlasticity.set_hardening_function defines isotropic hardening; function_type="power" gives R(p) = h * p**beta.
ElastoPlasticity.yield_function evaluates the von Mises yield function as von Mises stress minus the yield stress minus the hardening function of the plasticity.
In geometrically nonlinear analysis ElastoPlasticity returns the Kirchhoff stress and hands the Cauchy stress tau/J to the assembly, so its response matches Simcoon's EPICP UMAT.
The Simcoon class is the Fedoo adapter for Simcoon constitutive laws and is associated with fedoo.weakform.StressEquilibrium.
Simcoon's _ISOTROPIC_UMATS set includes the J2 plasticity laws EPICP, EPKCP and EPCHA among others.
The Simcoon EPICP UMAT is registered with n_statev = 8, props {E, nu, alpha, sigmaY, k, m} for the power law sigma_e = sigmaY + k*eps_p^m and statev {T:0, P:1, EP:slice(2,8)}.

Simcoon.from_modular builds a MODUL UMAT from a simcoon.modular.ModularMaterial (elasticity block + VonMisesYield + PowerLaw/LinearIsotropic/Voce hardening or Prager/ArmstrongFrederick/Chaboche kinematic terms).
Under finite strain a Simcoon modular material requires corate="log_r" (or "log_r_inc") in the stress-equilibrium weak form.
MechanicalUMAT is the base class for corotational user-material functions and owns the Fedoo-side constitutive lifecycle (state allocation, the UMAT call, stress/tangent conversion).
MechanicalUMAT has parameters use_elastic_tangent (default True, restores the initialization tangent at the start of every increment) and tangent_mode (default 1).
In finite strain the weak form owns and updates the deformation-gradient field, which MechanicalUMAT consumes as F0 and F1 and never overwrites.
MechanicalUMAT initial state variables can be assigned to an assembly before problem initialization via set_initial_statev.
The StressEquilibrium weak form can be used for 3D solids or with a 2D plane assumption (plane strain or plane stress) and accepts geometric nonlinearities via nlgeom in {True,'UL','TL'}.
The StressEquilibrium weak form default corate is "log_r" (logarithmic strain with the exact polar frame increment DR = R1 R0^T).
The incompressibility option "fbar" evaluates the volume change at the element center with a consistent non-symmetric tangent for quad4/hex8 (not available for 2Daxi or the total lagrangian method).
HourglassStiffness is the weak form that controls hourglass modes for reduced integration, based on Flanagan and Belytschko (1981), and is used with hex8/quad4 at one Gauss point.
The default hourglass_stiffness coefficient is 0.01, a compromise between suppressing hourglass modes and avoiding extra flexural stiffness.
StressEquilibriumRI combines StressEquilibrium with HourglassStiffness, uses one Gauss point by default and should only be used with hex8 or quad4 elements.
The NonLinear problem's nr_parameters default criterion is "Force" with tol=5e-3 and max_subiter=16.
The set_nr_criterion method signature has default criterion="Force", accepting criterion in ['Displacement','Force','Work'].
The set_nr_criterion docstring claims default = "Displacement", which is a documentation/code mismatch with the actual "Force" default.
For the "Displacement" NR criterion, when err0 is None it is computed from the current increment norm (plus 0.01*total displacement norm) so the criterion does not get progressively looser.
The nlsolve method solves the nonlinear problem with Newton-Raphson, supporting adaptive dt increase (x1.25) and decrease (x0.25) and a minimal time increment dt_min.

The to_start method restores the state of the last converged increment when the NR algorithm fails to converge, resetting the displacement increment and re-assembling the tangent at the restored state.
add_line_search adds a line-search (step-size alpha) for the NR solver with methods Armijo/Residual/Energy/Quadratic (default Quadratic) and modes natural/minimize/safeguard.
NonLinearNewmark is a convenience factory (beta=0.25, gamma=0.5) that creates a nonlinear Newmark problem; the mass is now derived from material density (set_density) or weakform.set_inertia.
Problem.add_output registers an output (file_format one of fdh5/fdz/vtk/msh/npz/csv/xlsx, output_type Node/Element/GaussPoint) for automatic saving by the solve methods.
Problem.save_results writes the current state to every registered output; in user-managed (manual) solution loops it must be called manually.
Problem.solve solves the linear system A X = B+D on the free dofs (via the backend set by set_solver).
Problem.apply_boundary_conditions(t_fact, t_fact_old) fills the Dirichlet increment vector, the Neumann force vector and builds the MPC elimination matrix and free-dof set.
Problem.init_bc_start_value is used only for incremental problems to set each BC's start value from the current displacement/force so the load ramps from the current state.
Problem.get_ext_forces returns the sum of external (Neumann), node reaction (Dirichlet) and inertia forces; for NonLinear it returns the latest evaluated residual balance.

Problem.set_solver supports 'direct' (pypardiso / python-mumps / petsc mumps / scipy spsolve), iterative methods (cg, bicg, gmres, ...) and explicit backends ('pardiso','mumps','direct_scipy','petsc') or a user function.

The official quick-start workflow is: import fedoo, define the modeling space, create/import the mesh, define weak formulations, create the Assembly, define the Problem and solver, solve, then analyse/export results.
The modeling space dimension can be '3D' or '2D' (plane), and may also be '2Dstress' for the plane-stress assumption.
For a direct solver the quick-start strongly recommends installing pypardiso (Intel), python-mumps (cross-platform) or petsc4py for better performance.

The test test_radial_return_matches_simcoon_simple_shear_reference feeds 20 proportional shear increments (gamma 0->0.02) and checks the final von Mises shear stress against the Simcoon EPICP reference value 314.581143696 MPa.
The same test asserts the final accumulated plasticity equals the Simcoon EPICP reference value 0.00918589977986.
The test uses material constants E = 200e3, NU = 0.3, SIGMA_Y = 300, H = 1000, BETA = 0.3 with a power hardening function.

test_finite_element_state_uses_mechanical_umat_labels_only verifies ElastoPlasticity exposes only MechanicalUMAT labels: props_label {young_modulus:0, poisson_ratio:1, yield_stress:2} and statev_label {P:0, EP:slice(1,7)}.
test_mechanical_umat_update_restarts_from_committed_state verifies a new trial re-integrates from the committed state (Newton rollback support at the material level).
test_corotational_update_transports_plastic_strain_with_dr verifies the EP plastic-strain history is transported by the corotational rotation DR under nlgeom="UL".
The verified 2DplasticBending.py run (fedoo 1.0.1) reports step-1 max von Mises 1121.06 MPa, final max von Mises 1144.60 MPa and springback 0.219 mm.

The Force criterion during the bending springback is stuck at a dt-independent normalized-error floor of 0.76755, so "Displacement" must be used (final state within 2.2e-4 mm of the exact zero-load equilibrium).
For the 4-node typeBending switch the verified 2D bending max von Mises is 1351.73 MPa, and the mat=0 linear-elastic switch gives Uy -> -0.0471.
The from-scratch model has 861 nodes / 800 quad4 (rectangle_mesh nx=41, ny=21, 16x2 mm, 2Dplane) and the bottom-right roller leaves Ux free = 1.605 mm at the end of loading.
At end of loading in the from-scratch run, the max accumulated plasticity P (EPICP statev[1], nodal) is 0.347769 at node 20 (8.0, 0.0).
The from-scratch run peak von Mises at end of loading is GP max 1057.4522 MPa and Node max 1061.2347 MPa.
After elastic release the from-scratch run has a permanent set (springback) of 0.2960 mm (Uy_tip -5.0 -> -4.704038).
The from-scratch final residual-stress peak is vm Node max 1067.7754 MPa.
The verified plastic_bending_3D.py run (fedoo 1.0.1) took 129.7 s with 40 NR increments at fixed dt=0.025.
The 3D bending model is a 16x2x10 mm box with 1029 nodes / 720 hex8, using NLGEOM="UL" and f-bar incompressibility.
The 3D bending peak von Mises is GP max 1242.7544 MPa and Node max 1332.8916 MPa.
The 3D bending end rotation at the simply-supported end is -0.7521 rad (-43.1 deg), consistent with a plastic-hinge state.
The 3D bending switches mat=0 (ELISO), mat=2 (ElastoPlasticity) and typeBending=4nodes were all construct-checked (not full-solve re-run) on fedoo 1.0.1.
The set_nr_criterion default in fedoo 1.0.1 is "Force" (nr_parameters["criterion"]="Force"), while the docstring claims default "Displacement" - a documented doc/code mismatch.
The Force criterion fails on kinematically-driven problems where ||F_ext|| ~ 0 (e.g. ~1.36e-11 on rotation_test.py) and the normalized error is stuck ~0.68-1.1.
The Force criterion also fails on force-relaxation-to-zero (springback), where the normalized residual has a dt-independent floor (0.76755 in the bending springback).
The "Displacement" criterion is verified for the bending springback (15 s PASS, final state within 2.2e-4 mm of the exact zero-load equilibrium).
Conversely the "Displacement" criterion stalls on some stiff force-driven contacts (Err ~ 0.04) where "Force" is the working choice.
The rotation_test.py validation (90 deg rigid 3D cube rotation) gives max |Disp| = 1.0 mm and max vm = 2.57e-10 MPa (rigid, zero strain).
The rotation_test fix required set_nr_criterion -> "Displacement" because the default "Force" fails (purely kinematically driven, ||F_ext|| ~ 1.36e-11).
The shear_test.py validation (1331 nodes hex8 simple shear) gives vm_max = 1295.31 MPa (GP), EP max = 1.40056, and mat=2 ElastoPlasticity cross-validates at 1295.309 MPa.
The torsion_test.py validation (180 deg torsion about X) gives mat=1 (EPICP) and mat=2 (ElastoPlasticity) vm_max = 1339.8 MPa (agreeing).
All 4 scripts in the plasticity/ folder (2DplasticBending, from-scratch, plastic_bending_3D and the rotation/shear/torsion validation tests) are verified PASS on fedoo 1.0.1.
The Main_documentation_fedoo/generated folder mirrors the autodoc API pages, covering 1,823 pages (one HTML page per class, function and member).
The documented fedoo.problem.* API classes include Linear, NonLinear, NonLinearNewmark, LinearNewmark, Modal, LinearBuckling, ExplicitDynamic, ProblemBase and Problem.
The documented fedoo.constitutivelaw.* classes include ElasticIsotrop, ElastoPlasticity, FE2 and Simcoon (among others).
The fedoo Python source docstrings are the authoritative API documentation source.
The current fedoo source version is 1.0.1, released 2026-10-01 per the CHANGELOG.
